title: Housing-assistance exit type predicts sharply different housing, health, and wage outcomes
source_unit: Heads of household and individuals exiting housing assistance in the HUD HEARS linked administrative-data study
geography: King County, Washington; Seattle Housing Authority and King County Housing Authority

observations.period: Nondeath, nontransfer exits; linked study cohort

denominator.unit: heads of household with classified exit type

positive_exit_share.unit: percent of heads of household; increased income, homeownership, or move to nonsubsidized rental among positive examples

negative_exit_share.unit: percent of heads of household; examples include eviction, lease violation, criminal activity, or abandonment

individual_linked_sample.unit: linked individuals with classified exit type

one_year_homelessness_positive_exit.unit: percent of individuals with a homelessness or unstable-housing event within one year after exit

one_year_homelessness_neutral_exit.unit: percent of individuals with a homelessness or unstable-housing event within one year after exit

one_year_homelessness_negative_exit.unit: percent of individuals with a homelessness or unstable-housing event within one year after exit

negative_exit_behavioral_health_crisis_o.unit: adjusted odds ratio versus neutral exit for a behavioral-health crisis within one year

positive_vs_negative_ed_odds.unit: adjusted odds ratio for one or more emergency-department visits within one year, positive versus negative exit

positive_exit_wage_premium.unit: dollars higher quarterly wages before and after exit for positive-exit households relative to other exit groups

observations.method: HUD Form 50058 and separate public-housing-authority exit records were probabilistically linked with King County employment-security wage data, Medicaid claims, behavioral-health data, homelessness-service data, and the Homeless Management Information System. Exit reasons were standardized as positive, neutral, or negative; outcomes were examined within one year after exit with adjusted comparisons.
observations.uncertainty: This is a regional observational study using probabilistic linkage and locally defined exit categories. The categories are substantively meaningful but not purely natural: health-related and moves-to-family exits can be positive or negative depending on circumstances. Associations do not establish that exit type caused the later outcome, and results may not generalize nationally or to non-MTW housing authorities.
observations.subgroup: Heads of household and linked individuals exiting from Seattle Housing Authority or King County Housing Authority assistance after excluding deaths and transfers between PHA programs.
observations.counterinterpretation: Pre-existing health, homelessness, income, housing-market, and administrative conditions may jointly influence both exit classification and later outcomes. The strong separation may therefore reflect selection into exit type as well as consequences of the exit.

related_sources.claim: HUD USER context describes the longstanding need to distinguish positive and negative housing-assistance exits.

boundary: This record supplies a same-linked-unit regional housing-exit-to-housing-stability, health, behavioral-health, and wage-outcome bridge. It does not provide a national estimate, causal exit effects, rent burden for every linked unit, household trust, political action, or durable security beyond the one-year outcome window.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Hash is of the canonical official PDF URL because HUD USER returned the report through the web document interface but denied a direct local PDF transfer; official report text and tables were reviewed. Restricted linked administrative data and analysis code are not retained.
